events.title: LDAP standardized
events.summary: RFC 1777 defined the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol in March 1995 — a TCP-based standard for querying and updating directory services.
events.about: LDAP models organizations as a tree of entries (users, groups, printers) with attributes like `cn`, `mail`, and `memberOf`. It replaced heavier X.500 DAP for most deployments and became the backbone of Active Directory, OpenLDAP, and corporate SSO. Every 'sign in with your company account' flow still traces back to directory lookups LDAP made universal.

narrative.whyChosen: LDAP turned enterprise directories into a simple, interoperable network protocol.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the standard way applications authenticate users and look up org structure at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Apps needed a lightweight way to read user and group data from centralized directories without proprietary APIs.

events.title: Ward Cunningham creates the wiki
events.summary: Ward Cunningham launched the first wiki in March 1995 — quick collaborative editing that inspired Wikipedia and countless internal dev docs.
events.about: Wiki syntax and culture ('edit this page') shaped how engineering teams document runbooks, RFCs, and postmortems. Cunningham's pattern language work also influenced agile and software design thinking.

narrative.whyChosen: The wiki invented lightweight collaborative documentation.
narrative.whyImportant: It lowered the barrier to contributing knowledge compared to formal CMS tools.
narrative.problemSolved: Team knowledge was trapped in email and individual files without shared editing.
